clue.text: A fabulous collection of asses a pleb groomed

indicators.note: something groomed has been tidied and rearranged, so these letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A tale of donkeys being brushed down by a commoner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'groomed' rearranges the twelve letters of OF ASSES A PLEB; asses and a groom also fit the beast-fable world of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek fabulist's moral tales form a famous anthology, so a collection of fables is literally fabulous.

clue.text: Stood up to welcome doctor who wrote of Hollywood lies

indicators.note: to welcome a guest is to take them in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: stood up means arose, got to one's feet
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's degree

explanation.surface: Someone rises to greet a physician who exposed Tinseltown's falsehoods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to welcome' signals a container. David Ambrose is a British novelist whose books include Hollywood Lies.
explanation.definitionFit: The British thriller writer David Ambrose published the novel Hollywood Lies.

clue.text: In which Pinkie has affair in south and Hale loses pound to maiden

indicators.note: Hale loses one letter to another, so one letter is swapped out for a new one

parts.note: taken as the name as written
L (libra) is the abbreviation for a pound
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: It sounds like a plot summary of Brighton Rock, where Pinkie and Hale both appear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loses ... to' swaps the pound for the maiden. Pinkie and Hale suggest Greene's Brighton Rock, but Pinkie Aurangzeb has her affair in Rushdie's novel.
explanation.definitionFit: In Salman Rushdie's novel of that title, Pinkie Aurangzeb conducts an affair with Omar Khayyam Shakil.

clue.text: A pianist playing ringing grand for Mohsin Hamid, say

indicators.note: ringing means encircling, so the reworked letters close round another piece
playing suggests the letters are played about with and rearranged

parts.note: K, for a thousand, is slang for a grand

explanation.surface: A pianist performs on a resonant grand piano for a novelist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' rearranges A PIANIST and 'ringing' puts K (a grand, a thousand pounds) inside that anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Mohsin Hamid, author of The Reluctant Fundamentalist, was born in Lahore and is an example of a writer from that country.

clue.text: Jumper Jim Smiley had and Phileas cut without right

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so one piece stands round the other
cut means trimmed, so the surname loses its last letter

parts.note: Phileas Fogg is the traveller of Around the World in Eighty Days

explanation.surface: A reading of a Mark Twain tale crossed with Jules Verne's traveller.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' trims FOGG to FOG and 'without' puts it round R. Jim Smiley owns the jumping amphibian in Twain's story about Calaveras County.
explanation.definitionFit: Dan'l Webster, the leaping pet in Twain's Celebrated Jumping story, is a green amphibian.

clue.text: Live with funny hombre, a scribe of satirical stuff

parts.note: to be is to live or exist

indicators.note: funny means odd or peculiar, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Living alongside a comic Spanish fellow who writes satire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'funny' rearranges HOMBRE into ERBOHM.
explanation.definitionFit: Max, the Edwardian caricaturist and author of Zuleika Dobson, was known for urbane parody and satire.

clue.text: Old flame associatedwith Irishman Oscar Wilde?

parts.note: an ex is a former lover
Pat (Patrick) is the stock name for an Irishman

explanation.surface: A former lover linked to the Irish wit Wilde.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks Wilde as an example: he died in exile in Paris.
explanation.definitionFit: Wilde spent his last years living abroad in France, an emigrant from his homeland.

clue.text: Knight and pawn English vicar moved onto third of files

parts.note: P is the chess abbreviation for a pawn

indicators.note: moved means shifted about, so the letters are rearranged
third of points to the third letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A chess move: a knight and a pawn, and a clergyman shifted onto a file.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moved' rearranges VICAR to RCIVA, and 'third of' takes L from FILES. The chess setting of knight, pawn and files is all surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Percival is one of the Arthurian Round Table, a mounted warrior of chivalry.

clue.text: Woman who cooked up horse, bit of speed and E competently

indicators.note: a bit of the word, its first letter, is taken

parts.note: taken as written
competently means well, ably

explanation.surface: A woman who rustled up a horse at speed, doing it ably.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bit of' takes S from SPEED; the clue lists S, E and WELL in that order. 'Cooked up' means invented: Anna Sewell wrote Black Beauty.
explanation.definitionFit: Anna Sewell invented the horse narrator of Black Beauty, her only novel.

clue.text: Gloomy traveller returning with Earl Melanter, perhaps

parts.note: gloomy means black, as in a black mood

indicators.note: returning means coming back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a Rom is a Romany traveller

explanation.surface: A gloomy wanderer comes back with an aristocrat named Melanter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns ROM into MOR. Melanter was the pen name under which the author of Lorna Doone first published poems, so 'perhaps' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: R.D. Blackmore issued his early verse under the pseudonym Melanter before writing Lorna Doone.

clue.text: Brazilian playmaker entertains European linesman

indicators.note: to entertain is to hold or host, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: Pelé was the great Brazilian footballer

explanation.surface: A famous Brazilian footballer plays host to a fellow from Europe who runs the line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entertains' puts E inside PELE. 'Linesman' is a football official on the surface but here means a writer of verse lines.
explanation.definitionFit: George Peele was an Elizabethan dramatist and poet, a maker of lines of verse.

clue.text: Lyrical works written about small area in port city

parts.note: odes are lyric poems

explanation.surface: Lyric poems composed about a little district in a harbour town.
explanation.definitionFit: The Black Sea city in Ukraine is a major seaport.

clue.text: "The greater the -, the more glory in overcoming it" (Molière)

definitions.text: "The greater the -, the more glory in overcoming it" (Molière)

parts.words: "The greater the -, the more glory in overcoming it" (Molière)
parts.note: a quotation with a gap: the missing word is the thing that stands in the way and must be overcome

explanation.surface: A quotation from Molière with one word left out.
explanation.definitionFit: Something one overcomes is a hindrance or barrier, the word Molière used in this line.

clue.text: Parisian with a flattering way starring in Seven Beauties

indicators.note: starring in a film means appearing within it, so the letters sit inside the title

explanation.surface: Someone from Paris with a charming manner appears in a Wertmüller film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starring in' signals the letters in sEVEN BEAUties. Seven Beauties is a 1975 Italian film by Lina Wertmüller.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase means in a favourable light, describing a flattering manner of presenting something.

clue.text: Herr Naphta is one porky Victor covered in ale

indicators.note: covered in means wrapped by, so the pieces go inside the drink

parts.note: ale is a kind of beer
porky (from rhyming slang pork pie) means a lie
V is Victor in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: A character from The Magic Mountain described as a fat winner doused in ale.
explanation.walkthrough: Porky is British rhyming slang: pork pie, lie. 'covered in' signals a container. Naphta is the Jesuit in Mann's The Magic Mountain.
explanation.definitionFit: Naphta, Mann's Jesuit-trained zealot, is a man of fervent faith.

clue.text: "We did not care: we knew we were / -'s Own Brigade" (Wilde)

definitions.text: "We did not care: we knew we were / -'s Own Brigade" (Wilde)

parts.words: "We did not care: we knew we were / -'s Own Brigade" (Wilde)
parts.note: a gapped line from The Ballad of Reading Gaol: the missing words name the prince of hell whose brigade the prisoners were

explanation.surface: A line from Wilde's prison ballad with a gap to fill.
explanation.definitionFit: In Wilde's poem the convicts call themselves the brigade of Satan, the fiend of hell.

clue.text: On top of shelf, Twilight's left with a Nobel winner's debut

indicators.note: in a down entry, being on something means sitting above it, so the other pieces come before

parts.note: twilight is dusk; the 's is a link
with means and, in addition

indicators.note: the top of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Twilight, the vampire novel, is left with others on the top bookshelf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top of' gives S from SHELF, and 'On' puts the rest above it in this down entry. Twilight looks like the vampire novel but means dusk.
explanation.definitionFit: J.M. Coetzee, the 2003 Nobel laureate, made his first appearance in fiction with this 1974 book.

clue.text: A month in which you see your setter's artistic beauty

indicators.note: the pieces are things in which something else is seen, so another piece goes inside them

parts.note: March is a month
the setter speaking of themself says my

explanation.surface: A month when the setter reveals their own pretty painter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in which you see' signals that the setter's word sits inside 'A month'.
explanation.definitionFit: The youngest March sister in Little Women is the vain, pretty one who wants to be a painter.

clue.text: God appears in leaves in Tennessee, possibly

indicators.note: to appear in something is to show up within it, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: to leave in a testament is to will, so leaves means wills
I AM is God's name for himself in Exodus

explanation.surface: God shows up among the foliage of a southern state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appears in' signals a container. 'Leaves' looks like foliage but is the verb of bequeathing.
explanation.definitionFit: Tennessee is the playwright's first name, so he is one bearer of the surname.

clue.text: Hardy area of land with borders for eggplants and greens

indicators.note: the borders of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: greens is British slang for sexual intercourse

explanation.surface: A gardener's plot where aubergines and vegetables grow along the edges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'borders for' takes the first and last letters of EGGPLANTS, E and S. Greens is British slang for sex. Hardy set his novels in a fictional West Country region.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Hardy revived the old Anglo-Saxon kingdom's name for the fictional region of his novels.

clue.text: I successfully pitched drug for potion-drinking royal

parts.note: a salesman who pitches successfully has sold
E is the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A salesman boasts of having peddled a drug to a princess who drinks a potion.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'potion-drinking royal' is the Irish princess who shares the love potion with Tristan.
explanation.definitionFit: In the legend and in Wagner's opera, the Irish princess drinks a love philtre with Tristan.

clue.text: English sermon affectedthoughtful writer

indicators.note: affected means altered or worked on, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An English preacher's address moves a reflective author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'affected' rearranges SERMON into MERSON.
explanation.definitionFit: Ralph Waldo, the American Transcendentalist essayist, was a reflective philosopher-author.

clue.text: Edith Granger is one of these tramps keeping quiet

definitions.text: Edith Granger is one of these

indicators.note: keeping means holding, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: to tramp is to step heavily, so tramps means steps
mum means silent, as in keep mum

explanation.surface: Vagrants keep silent about a Dickens character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeping' signals a container. Edith Granger marries Mr Dombey in Dickens's Dombey and Son, becoming Florence's stepmother.
explanation.definitionFit: As Dombey's second wife, Edith becomes second mother to his daughter Florence, a parent by marriage.

clue.text: Musical theme in books provided by head of music

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: OT, the Old Testament, is a collection of books
provided means if, on condition that

explanation.surface: A melody found in books, supplied by the director of music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head of' gives M from MUSIC, which leads the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A recurring melodic figure in a composition is its leitmotif or subject.

clue.text: What Dr Rieux fought in capital city changing hands

indicators.note: the hands are right and left, so R is changed for L

parts.note: Prague is the Czech capital

explanation.surface: A doctor's struggle in a European capital where things change hands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changing hands' swaps R (right) for L (left) in PRAGUE. Dr Rieux is the doctor in Camus's novel set in Oran.
explanation.definitionFit: In Camus's novel Dr Rieux battles the epidemic of bubonic disease in Oran.

clue.text: German dictionary founder and lawmaker is ghastly, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly means as spoken, so the word sounds like another

parts.note: ghastly means grim, dreadful

explanation.surface: A grim German legislator who started a dictionary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reportedly' gives a word sounding like GRIM. Jacob Grimm began the Deutsches Wörterbuch and formulated a law of sound change in Germanic languages.
explanation.definitionFit: Jacob, the elder of the fairy-tale brothers, began the great German dictionary and gave his name to a sound law.

clue.text: Money-making man intends to put one down

indicators.note: to put a letter somewhere new means it is moved within the word
in a down entry, down means lower, so the letter moves later in the word

parts.note: intends means aims
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A greedy man who means to dispatch someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to put ... down' moves the I of AIMS lower, giving AMIS. Martin Amis wrote the novel Money.
explanation.definitionFit: Martin Amis wrote the 1984 novel Money, so he is the man who made it.

clue.text: Passage written on The End of the Affair

indicators.note: in an across entry, written on means written after, so this piece follows
the end of a word is its last letter

parts.note: a vent is a passage for air or gas

explanation.surface: A passage annotated on a copy of Greene's The End of the Affair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'End of' takes E from THE, and 'written on' puts VENT after it. The Greene title is all surface.
explanation.definitionFit: An affair in the sense of a happening or occasion is an occurrence.

clue.text: People like Byron repelled masculine men with grotesque acts

indicators.note: repelled means driven back, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: OR, other ranks, means ordinary soldiers or men
antics are grotesque or absurd capers

explanation.surface: Lord Byron's sort recoiled from macho men behaving absurdly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repelled' turns M and OR round to ROM.
explanation.definitionFit: Byron was a leading poet of the early nineteenth-century movement of feeling and imagination, alongside Shelley and Keats.

clue.text: Levi's product a misfithas in for alterations

indicators.note: sent for alterations means to be changed, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A badly fitting pair of Levi's jeans goes back to be altered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for alterations' rearranges A MISFIT HAS IN. Levi is Primo Levi, author of the Auschwitz memoir, not the jeans maker.
explanation.definitionFit: Primo Levi wrote this memoir of his imprisonment at Auschwitz.
